properties.description: Carinthia has a constitutionally recognized Slovene-speaking minority (bilingual place-name signage, historically contested); shown as an identity-layer note on this record rather than a separate territorial claim.

Vorarlberg sits within the cross-border Alemannic dialect continuum linking it to eastern Switzerland, southern Baden and Alsace -- a genuine identity layer that cuts across the AT/CH/DE/FR state borders modeled elsewhere in this dataset as separate regions. Shown as an independently toggleable overlay rather than redrawn territory.

Neuchatel and Jura (and parts of Fribourg) are francophone cantons statistically grouped into the German-plurality 'Espace Mittelland' macro-region; the Romandie/German-Swiss linguistic boundary (the Roestigraben) runs through this region rather than around it. Shown as an independently toggleable overlay.

The French Basque Country (Iparralde/Pays Basque) forms a cultural micro-layer within Pyrénées-Atlantiques (FRI15), alongside the distinct, non-Basque Béarnais territory in the same département. A unified cross-border Basque region (Euskadi + Navarre + Iparralde) is modeled in zone3 ('basque-unified', shown via the zone3 basque variant set), reusing this NUTS-3 code without altering Aquitaine's own boundaries here.

Corsica carries an active, unresolved autonomy/identity conflict distinct from the zone's other regions: a nationalist movement historically included an armed insurgency (FLNC, ceasefire 2014) and now holds a governing mainstream-autonomist majority in the territorial assembly, seeking expanded self-government and constitutional recognition of the Corsican people. Flagged as a toggleable identity-conflict layer over the whole region rather than resolved either way.

Eupen-Malmedy (Bezirk Verviers, the German-speaking Community of Belgium) is a small but constitutionally recognized third linguistic community embedded within Wallonia/Liège province, with its own parliament and government. Flagged as a toggleable micro-cultural layer distinct from the surrounding French-speaking Walloon identity, without redrawing Wallonia's own boundaries.

Dutch Limburg's Ripuarian/Low Franconian dialect continuum (Limburgish, a recognized regional language) extends across the Dutch-German border into neighboring North Rhine-Westphalia, forming a German-Dutch border micro-cultural zone around Maastricht-Heerlen-Aachen distinct from the rest of Zuid-Nederland. Flagged as a toggleable cross-border micro-layer per the zone brief's mandate.

The only available NUTS-3 unit covering Iparralde (French Basque Country) is FRI15 (Pyrénées-Atlantiques), which covers the ENTIRE department including Béarn — a substantial, distinct, non-Basque (Occitan/Gascon-speaking) territory to the east, not a minor edge effect. Using FRI15 therefore materially over-states the unified Basque region's French-side extent. geoBoundaries France ADM3 (arrondissement de Bayonne) is a concrete, checkable finer-resolution alternative that would map much more closely to true Iparralde — noted as the recommended next geometry source for the pipeline, not integrated in this content-only pass.

Valle d'Aosta/Vallée d'Aoste (ITC2) is a bilingual French-Italian special-autonomy region with its own statute, distinct from Piedmontese identity, folded into this record for population/urban-hub scale (~123,000 residents, no independent metro of dataset-relevant size). Toggleable as a separate micro-region if finer granularity is adopted.
Morocco claims sovereignty over both Ceuta and Melilla as territories to be decolonized/reintegrated; Spain administers them as autonomous cities. Flagged, not adjudicated.

Spain claims sovereignty over Gibraltar (ceded to Britain in perpetuity under the 1713 Treaty of Utrecht, but Spain disputes this); Gibraltarians have twice rejected shared/Spanish sovereignty by referendum (1967, 2002). Flagged, not adjudicated.

Historically, Comunidad de Madrid was carved out of 'New Castile'/La Mancha territory (formalized 1833, autonomous community 1983). This composite deliberately excludes Madrid to preserve the site's Catalonia-Madrid flagship framing; a historically 'fuller' Castile would include it. Flagged rather than silently resolved.

Using full NUTS-3 provinces (Segovia, Ávila, Guadalajara, Toledo) rather than finer municipal/comarca geometry means this record includes large rural areas of each province far outside any realistic daily-commute shed of Madrid. No finer NUTS geometry is available in the index; flagged rather than silently corrected, matching the existing basque-unified/FRI15 precedent.

Sápmi, the Indigenous Sámi homeland, spans northern Finland, Sweden and Norway and is not congruent with any national or NUTS boundary. This overlay flags the cross-border cultural area without redrawing national region boundaries; it may overlap the nuts_codes of the Norrland, Tromsø/North and other neighboring regions.

Sapmi, the Indigenous Sami homeland, spans northern Finland, Sweden and Norway and is not congruent with any national or NUTS boundary. This is the Swedish-side reference to the same cross-border cultural area already flagged canonically as 'sapmi-cross-border' on fi-lapland-sapmi (given a distinct id here per the project's global conflict_flag-id-uniqueness rule); it flags the overlay without redrawing national region boundaries.
Silesian (Ślązacy) ethnolinguistic self-identification, contested minority-recognition status; 2021 census self-declarations (596,224 nationwide) concentrated in the Katowice conurbation.
Kashubian (Kaszëbë) ethnolinguistic minority with recognized regional-language status since 2005, concentrated in the rural hinterland southwest of the Tricity.
Kashubian ethnolinguistic minority, recognized regional-language status since 2005 (split-view duplicate of pl-pomerania's pl-kashubia flag, renamed for global conflict_flag-id uniqueness).

Polish national minority in the Zaolzie/Těšín Silesia area on the Czech side of the historic Cieszyn Silesia partition — a cross-border Silesian-identity layer distinct from the Moravian census self-identification recorded elsewhere in Czechia.

The historic Duchy of Silesia was partitioned between Prussia/Germany and Austria-Hungary/Czechoslovakia; today's Polish-Czech border bisects a continuous coal/steel industrial basin and Silesian-ethnolect dialect continuum. Shown as a toggleable unified view, not a territorial claim.
Rusyn/Ukrainian national minority concentrated in the northeastern Prešov region, with its own recognized minority-language status distinct from the Slovak national majority.

Recognized Italian national minority in Istria with official bilingual status (Croatian-Italian) in coastal towns, and a distinct regionalist political tradition (IDS/DDI) advocating autonomy within Croatia.

Székely Land / Hungarian-minority overlay retained per the mandated instruction even though the territory is now its own visible unit (ro-szekely-land): this flag marks the historic Transylvania-wide Hungarian/Saxon minority layer that predates and exceeds the modern Covasna/Harghita/Mureș county boundaries (e.g. Cluj and Târgu Mureș itself have long-standing Hungarian urban populations outside the three carved-out counties).

Live, organized Székely/Hungarian territorial-autonomy movement (Szekler National Council; periodic autonomy-day demonstrations; own flag) seeking self-government within Romania. Romania's central government has consistently rejected territorial-autonomy proposals; no legal Székely Land entity exists. Shown as an identity/political layer on this unit, not a redrawn or seceded territory.

Officially-recognized Muslim minority (Turkish, Pomak, Roma) protected under the 1923 Treaty of Lausanne, concentrated in the Xanthi-Komotini-Rodopi area — Greece's only legally recognized religious (not just ethnic) minority, a live and occasionally diplomatically sensitive Greek-Turkish bilateral issue.

De facto division since the 1974 Turkish intervention: the Republic of Cyprus (EU member, government-controlled ~63% of the island, modeled here) vs. the self-declared, Turkey-only-recognized 'Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus' (~37%), separated by the UN-patrolled Green Line (itself bisecting Nicosia). NO CLEAN GEOMETRY SOURCE EXISTS for a north/south sub-division (see identity_basis for the documented 5-minute geometry check: GISCO whole-island-only; geoBoundaries CYP ADM1's 6 districts predate 1974 and are themselves split by the line). North/south split explicitly PENDING a better geometry source — a deliberate, stated limitation, not a silently-resolved one.

Internal entity boundaries from the 1995 Dayton Peace Agreement. Now modeled as three separate cultural units (ba-federation-bih, ba-republika-srpska, ba-brcko-district) rather than one region with an overlay flag, per the parliament rule (each entity has a real constitutional legislature) — SUPERSEDES v0.1.0's single-unit-with-flag treatment, which itself argued the Dayton partition was 'not organic regionalism'. That argument is preserved in the zone notes as background even though the mandate has changed: the three units exist because of real, current constitutional government, independent of whether the original 1995 partition was organic.

Republika Srpska's entity-level leadership has periodically floated further autonomy or secession referenda (most prominently under President Milorad Dodik); no such move has legal effect under Bosnia's constitution or international law, and Republika Srpska remains a constituent entity of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Flagged as a live political fact distinct from the more settled Vojvodina/Federation cases.

Serb-majority North Mitrovica and adjacent municipalities remain a live flashpoint (parallel Serbian-backed institutions, periodic unrest, EU/NATO-mediated normalization talks); a distinct minority-conflict layer within the single-unit treatment, not modeled as a separate geometry given Kosovo's own single-unit exception status.

The Russian Federation unilaterally annexed Crimea (Autonomous Republic of Crimea + Sevastopol) in March 2014 following an internationally unrecognised referendum; the UN General Assembly (Resolution 68/262) and the vast majority of states continue to recognise Crimea as Ukrainian sovereign territory under military occupation. Included here on that basis, with occupation status flagged as an independently toggleable layer.
